instrument: DGS2 minus DE sovereign Svensson 2.0-year zero-coupon spot
transform: 5 common observation intervals, change of spread in bp

provenance.series: H.15 RIFLGFCY02_N.B and Bundesbank BBSIS 2.0-year Svensson spot
provenance.clock_statement: The Bundesbank serves the daily Svensson curve with its own `last update` stamp: the file fetched on 2026-11-20 reads `last update,2026-11-19 12:22:17` and already carries the 2026-11-19 value, so the curve is refreshed on the observation day itself. That single stamp is not proof of how the file behaved in 2024, and no Bundesbank release-time statement can be cited, so the reconstruction assumes nothing from it: a value dated T is treated as available only at 23:59 Europe/Berlin on T+1. The assumption can never outrun a next-morning refresh, it is 35.6 hours later than the only refresh this project has observed, and the cost is one day of lag, not a missing session.

clock_evidence.stated_by: Bundesbank BBSIS CSV header `last update` field, read 2026-11-20
clock_evidence.bound: 23:59 Europe/Berlin on the day after the observation date
clock_evidence.receipt: none - a bound is not a receipt

provenance.transform_note: The spread is differenced on dates both publishers produced and only then changed over five intervals. No date is filled, bridged or borrowed from one publisher alone.
